subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Where in the Indian Gondwana sequence is the Permian-Triassic boundary placed stratigraphically?
options: In Gondwana: top of Raniganj Formation. Panchet Formation overlies
Top of Panchet where it is overlain by the marine Supra-Panchet beds
Top of Barakar where it is overlain by the Barren Measures succession
Top of Mahadeva sandstone where it passes into the Lower Gondwana coal
solution: P-T boundary: extinction event. In Kashmir: Guryul Ravine (marine section).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In what order do minerals precipitate in an evaporite sequence as solubility increases?
options: Carbonate → gypsum → halite → K-Mg salts (increasing solubility)
Halite → gypsum → carbonate → K-Mg salts (in order of decreasing solubility)
K-Mg salts → halite → gypsum → carbonate (in order of decreasing solubility)
Carbonate → halite → K-Mg salts → gypsum (in order of increasing solubility)
solution: Evaporites: restricted basin, high evaporation. Zechstein, Mediterranean Messinian.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A counterclockwise P-T path, involving heating then burial, typically reflects which metamorphic history?
options: Heating→burial→exhumation. Contact metamorphism overprinted by regional
Burial→heating→exhumation typical of continental collision orogens
Isothermal decompression following rapid crustal burial and continental collision
Clockwise loop passing repeatedly through the same P-T conditions
solution: CCW: high T first, then P increase. Plume-related metamorphism. Cordierite+andalusite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The magnitude of an earthquake is commonly expressed on the:
options: Richter (magnitude) scale
Mohs scale of mineral hardness
Beaufort scale of wind speed
pH scale of aqueous acidity
solution: Earthquake size is reported as magnitude (Richter / moment magnitude).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ore reserve classification (JORC): indicated resource requires:
options: Sufficient exploration for geological confidence but lower than measured
Surface exposure of the orebody without any sampling carried out beneath it
No drilling, with tonnage estimated purely from regional geological extrapolation
Any level of confidence, including purely speculative regional analogies
solution: Indicated: enough data for planning. Inferred: limited data. Measured: high confidence.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: After 3 half-lives, the percentage of the original radioactive parent isotope remaining is:
solution: Fraction remaining = (1/2)^3 = 12.5%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A bed dipping at 60° shows a width of 10 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
options: 5 m
solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 10×sin60° ≈ 8.66 m.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A 4 m seam over 4 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.85. The mineable reserve is about:
solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 4M m²×4×1.4×0.85 ≈ 19 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In coastal aquifers, the depth of the freshwater-saltwater interface below sea level is given by the Ghyben-Herzberg relation as:
options: Freshwater-saltwater interface. Ghyben-Herzberg: z = 40·h (h = head above sea level)
z = 80h giving an interface depth that is twice the Ghyben-Herzberg value of the site area
z = 20h giving an interface depth that is half the Ghyben-Herzberg value
z = h meaning the interface lies at exactly the same depth as the measured head value above sea level
solution: Ghyben-Herzberg: z = ρ_f·h/(ρ_s-ρ_f). For ρ_s/ρ_f = 1.025: z ≈ 40h.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What type of twinning is characteristic of the mineral plagioclase feldspar?
options: Polysynthetic (albite law) — repeated lamellae
Carlsbad simple twinning observed in potassium feldspars only
Cross twins characteristic of staurolite and aragonite
Simple twins formed during rapid magmatic crystallization
solution: Polysynthetic twinning diagnostic of plagioclase under microscope.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: On what basis are arcuate, bird-foot and estuarine deltas classified from one another?
options: Deltas form only where the river dominates over tide and wave
All deltas have identical shapes regardless of sediment supply
Deltas form only where wave action dominates over the river input
Arcuate (Nile), Birdfoot (Mississippi), Estuarine (Ganges)
solution: Delta: river sediment deposition at coast. Tidal/wave influence shapes delta type.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which active remote sensing technique uses laser scanning to produce high-resolution elevation data and can penetrate a vegetation canopy?
options: Laser scanning. High-resolution DEM. Penetrates vegetation canopy
Passive optical sensing of the solar radiation that is reflected from the ground surface
Thermal sensing of the emitted longwave infrared radiation from the surface of the ground
Synthetic aperture radar, which operates at the microwave radio wavelengths range
solution: LiDAR: 3D point cloud. Bare earth DEM. Used for fault mapping, forestry, flood modeling.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is a foreign rock fragment (enclave) enclosed within an igneous rock?
options: Gas bubble trapped in lava that later becomes filled with zeolites
Early-formed crystal that grew during the first stage of cooling
Foreign rock fragment in igneous rock. Enclave
Phenocryst of olivine or pyroxene in a porphyritic volcanic rock
solution: Xenolith: wall rock fragment. Used to study mantle composition and crustal contamination.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How do marine transgression and regression differ in their effects on the sedimentary record?
options: Transgression: sea advances (fining up). Regression: sea retreats (coarsening up)
Transgression: sea retreats and coarsens upward. Regression: sea advances and fines upward
A drop in sea level always produces a fining-upward transgressive succession
Transgression produces a coarsening-upward sequence and regression a fining-upward one
solution: Transgressive: sandstone → shale → limestone. Regressive: limestone → shale → sandstone.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Geophysical well logging lowers instruments into a borehole to measure what about the surrounding formations?
options: Physical properties of formations surrounding borehole
The magnetic field of the earth above the ground along a line
Acoustic velocity of the air between the rig and road cuts
Density of the atmosphere as a function of altitude at the site
solution: Well logging: lowered tools measure resistivity, density, sonic, gamma ray, neutron. Identifies lithology, fluids.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How are the strike and dip of an inclined geological surface defined, and what does each measure?
options: Strike: the angle of steepest descent. Dip: the compass bearing of the horizontal line
Strike: vertical line on the plane. Dip: angle measured horizontally along the strike
Strike: a horizontal line; Dip: the compass direction of that line, always parallel to it
Strike: trend of horizontal line on inclined plane. Dip: angle to horizontal
solution: Strike: compass direction. Dip: angle + direction (e.g., 30° SE).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A mineral specimen of mass 54 g has a volume of 20 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
solution: SG = mass/volume = 54/20 = 2.7.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following is a common rockfall protection measure?
options: Only the removal of the source block by controlled blasting of the cliff face
Only warning sirens with no physical protection measure at all
Only regrading of the slope to a gentler uniform angle
Barrier, catch ditch, mesh, rock bolt, shotcrete. Warning systems
solution: Rockfall: netting (draped, anchored). Attenuator barriers. Risk: exposure × probability × consequence.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which physical and chemical changes after deposition constitute diagenesis of sedimentary rocks?
options: Physical/chemical changes after deposition, before metamorphism (compaction, cementation, dissolution)
Metamorphism: solid-state recrystallization of minerals under high pressure and temperature within the crust
Weathering and erosion of exposed rocks at the Earth's surface by wind and water
Partial melting of crustal rocks followed by crystallization of new igneous minerals
solution: Diagenesis: near-surface, low T (<200°C). Cementation: quartz overgrowths, calcite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following lists typical groundwater quality parameters assessed against WHO/BIS standards?
options: Only the pH value of the groundwater in the region being tested
Only the colour, taste and odour of the water sample
TDS, pH, hardness, Cl, NO₃, Fe, F, As. WHO/BIS standards
Only the turbidity measured with a nephelometer in NTU
solution: Fluoride: 0.5-1.5 mg/L. Arsenic: <0.01 mg/L. Nitrate: <45 mg/L. TDS: <500 mg/L.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Magmatic ore deposits: chromitite layers in layered intrusions formed by:
options: Precipitation of chromite from hot circulating hydrothermal brines
Settling of chromite crystals from basaltic magma
Mechanical concentration of chromite grains in stream placers
Lateritic enrichment of chromite by deep tropical weathering
solution: Layered intrusions: Bushveld, Stillwater. Chromitite: cumulate layers. Chromite settles from magma.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A rock sample of 100 cm³ contains 15 cm³ of pore space. Its porosity is:
solution: Porosity = (void volume/total volume)×100 = 15/100 = 15%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is a small vug in granite with inward-facing crystals, formed by late-stage volatiles?
options: Small vug in granite with inward-facing crystals. Late-stage volatiles
Void produced by the weathering of feldspar grains along grain boundaries and cleavage planes
Cavity left by the dissolution of a fossil shell during diagenesis
Gas vesicle formed in lava by expansion of volatiles during eruption
solution: Miarolitic: miarolitic texture. Crystal-lined cavities. Indicates shallow emplacement.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Sinkholes, caves, underground streams and tower karst develop in limestone regions through which dominant process?
options: Landforms built by the deposition of sediment carried by river water in the floodplain area
Landforms produced by the wind erosion and deposition of sand and dust in arid desert regions of the world
Dissolution of limestone → sinkholes, caves, underground streams, tower karst
Landforms carved by the erosive action of moving glacier ice over the bedrock surface below
solution: Karst: CaCO₃ dissolved by carbonic acid. Cockpit karst, cone karst, tower karst.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How do stalactites and stalagmites differ in their position and direction of growth within a cave?
options: Stalactite grows upward from the floor of the cave and stalagmite from the ceiling
Both stalactite and stalagmite grow from the floor
Both stalactite and stalagmite grow from the ceiling
Stalactite: hangs from ceiling. Stalagmite: grows from floor
solution: Stalactite: CaCO₃ precipitation. Stalagmite: below dripline. Column: when they meet.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which radar technique measures millimetre-scale ground deformation and is applied to earthquakes, volcanoes, and subsidence studies?
options: Multispectral optical imaging that measures reflected radiation for land cover classification
Interferometric SAR. Measures ground deformation (mm-scale). Earthquake, volcano, subsidence
Optical stereoscopy using overlapping photographs to generate detailed elevation models of the surface
Thermal remote sensing of emitted radiation for mapping surface temperature variations
solution: InSAR: two radar images of same area. Phase difference = displacement. Sentinel-1.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which twin laws are commonly observed in the mineral plagioclase feldspar?
options: Albite (polysynthetic), pericline, Carlsbad (simple twin)
Random twins that show no relation to the crystal lattice
No twinning occurs in any plagioclase feldspar variety
Only interpenetration twins found in quartz and corundum
solution: Plagioclase: polysynthetic twinning diagnostic in thin section. Lamellae under crossed polars.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Differential Thermal Analysis (DTA) detects:
options: Chemical composition by elemental emission spectroscopy
Crystal structure refinement using X-ray diffraction
Phase transitions and dehydration reactions
Grain size distribution through sieve analysis and settling
solution: DTA: measures temperature difference between sample and reference. Exothermic/endothermic peaks.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 50 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.05. The Darcy velocity is:
options: 2.5 m/day
5 m/day
50 m/day
1000 m/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal seam covers 1 km², is 2 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 5.2 Mt
2 Mt
1.3 Mt
2.6 Mt
solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 1×10⁶ m²×2 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 2.6 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Finite strain ellipsoid: X≥Y≥Z. Stretch S = L/L₀. For simple shear γ=1:
options: X/Z ≈ 1
X/Z ≈ 3
solution: Simple shear γ=1: X/Z = γ+√(γ²+1) = 1+√2 ≈ 2.41. Strain ratio R=X/Y.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: On a streak plate, what colour does the mineral limonite typically produce?
options: Brownish yellow
Greenish black
Yellowish brown
Pale grey
solution: Limonite (FeO(OH)·nH2O) — yellow-brown streak. Hydrous iron oxide.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In an excavation below the water table, the heave (quick) condition develops when the upward seepage force:
options: The flow of water is entirely absent from the floor of the excavation
Water flows downward through the floor of the excavation
Upward water pressure exceeds effective stress. Quick condition
The soil is compressed by the weight of the overlying layers
solution: Heave: in sand near excavation. Critical gradient ~1. Sheet pile depth for safety.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In the faulted block shown, the hanging wall has moved up over the footwall. This is a:
options: Normal fault produced by extensional tectonic stress
Detachment fault with low-angle listric geometry
Strike-slip fault with dominantly horizontal displacement
Reverse fault (compressional)
solution: Hanging wall up = reverse fault, caused by compression.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Radiocarbon (C-14) dating is applicable to organic material up to what maximum age, and what does it require?
options: ¹⁴C (T½ = 5730 yr). For organic material <50 ka. Atmospheric production, calibration curve
U-Pb method applied to zircon crystals extracted from the same strata body being studied, for ancient rocks
Rb-Sr method applied to whole-rock samples of the basement crystalline rocks below
K-Ar method applied to potassium minerals of the volcanic ash beds that are present
solution: C-14: radiocarbon. β⁻ decay. Libby (1949). Calibration: tree rings, corals, speleothems.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which rocks are formed from volcanic ejecta such as ash, lapilli, bombs, and blocks?
options: Formed from volcanic ejecta (ash, lapilli, bombs, blocks)
Plutonic rocks crystallised slowly at depth from granitic magma
Metamorphic rocks produced by regional high-pressure metamorphism
Lava flows that solidify into massive aphanitic or glassy bodies
solution: Tuff (ash), lapillistone, agglomerate (bombs). Welded tuff = ignimbrite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+35+15) = 42%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Blueschist facies: key mineral glaucophane:
options: Green Ca-amphibole (hornblende). Stable at moderate P and T
Black Fe-amphibole. Characteristic of contact aureoles
White K-mica. Diagnostic of Barrovian metamorphic zones
Blue Na-amphibole. Stable at high P, low T (subduction)
solution: Glaucophane: Na₂(Mg₃Al₂)Si₈O₂₂(OH)₂. Blue color. Subduction zone metamorphism.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is an intrusive igneous body smaller than a batholith (<100 km²)?
options: Igneous body that is exactly the same size as a batholith in outcrop area
Intrusion larger than a batholith extending over hundreds of square km
Volcanic landform built of lava flows and pyroclastic material around a vent
Smaller than batholith (<100 km²)
solution: Stock: similar to batholith but smaller. Often associated with mineral deposits.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Banded iron formation records precipitation of what materials, and in which type of environment?
options: Precipitation of iron and silica from seawater
Metamorphic segregation of iron from mafic host rocks
Submarine volcanic eruption of iron-rich lava flows
Biological fixation of iron by ancient photosynthetic organisms
solution: BIF: alternating iron-rich and silica-rich layers. ~2.5-1.8 Ga.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 8% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+20+8) = 68%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Gneissic banding refers to which textural feature in high-grade metamorphic rocks?
options: Alignment of platy mica minerals along parallel planes
Alternating light (felsic) and dark (mafic) mineral layers
Random orientation of mineral grains without any layering
Lineation defined by elongate minerals parallel to the fold axis
solution: Gneiss: high grade. Segregation into bands. Compositional layering.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The Earth's outer core is inferred to be liquid because:
options: S-waves cannot pass through it
P-waves cannot pass through it
Both P- and S-waves speed up there
Neither wave reaches it
solution: Shear (S) waves cannot travel through liquids, creating an S-wave shadow zone — evidence of a liquid outer core.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which preprocessing step removes geometric distortions using ground control points and produces a map-projected, orthorectified image?
options: Resampling the image, using only the scene corner coordinates that are provided within the metadata file
Assigning the map coordinates only approximately, and accepting the large residual errors that result from it
Applying a standard map projection to the image, without correcting for the sensor-induced distortion
Remove geometric distortions. Map projection. GCPs. RMSE < 1 pixel. Orthorectification
solution: Geometric: model sensor + terrain. GCP: ground control points. Resampling: nearest, bilinear, cubic.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Mohr circle for stress: center = (σ₁+σ₃)/2, radius = (σ₁-σ₃)/2. For σ₁=100MPa, σ₃=40MPa:
options: Center=50MPa, radius=50MPa
Center=70MPa, radius=30MPa
Center=70MPa, radius=60MPa
Center=40MPa, radius=30MPa

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In GIS, landslide susceptibility mapping commonly uses a weighted overlay of which factors such as slope, geology, rainfall, and land use?
options: Analysis that uses a single factor only, such as the slope gradient being considered alone
Weighted overlay: slope, geology, rainfall, land use, distance to faults
The distance to rivers only, while ignoring the geology and land use factors entirely
Rainfall intensity that is recorded over just a single monsoon season period
solution: Susceptibility: heuristic, statistical (logistic regression), deterministic (infinite slope). Machine learning.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What in-situ parameter is obtained from a pressuremeter test?
options: In-situ stress-strain behavior. Modulus, limit pressure, creep pressure
A laboratory test on undisturbed samples to measure Atterberg limits
A cone penetration test (CPT) measuring tip resistance and sleeve friction ratio
A vane shear test measuring only the undrained shear strength of clay
solution: Pressuremeter: expandable probe in borehole. Ménard pressuremeter. P_0, P_f, P_l.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Freeze-thaw, exfoliation and salt crystal growth are physical processes, whereas dissolution, oxidation and hydrolysis belong to which class?
options: Weathering consists only of frost action acting on exposed rock surfaces in the cold climatic regions of the world today
Weathering consists only of the hydrolysis of silicate minerals taking place within the soil as the sole chemical weathering process in operation
Weathering consists only of the mechanical wedging of rock by plant roots growing in the cracks of the rock
Physical (freeze-thaw, exfoliation, salt crystal growth) and chemical (dissolution, oxidation, hydrolysis)
solution: Physical: mechanical breakup. Chemical: mineral alteration. Spheroidal weathering of jointed rock.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 10 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The Darcy velocity is:
options: 0.4 m/day
10 m/day
500 m/day
0.2 m/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: According to the Von Mises yield criterion, plastic deformation begins when the deviatoric stress components satisfy which condition?
options: Yielding occurs when the maximum principal stress reaches the uniaxial yield strength σ_y
Yielding when the maximum shear stress equals half the tensile yield strength in a tension test
Yielding when (σ₁-σ₂)²+(σ₂-σ₃)²+(σ₃-σ₁)² ≥ 2σ_y²
Yielding occurs when total strain energy per unit volume attains a critical threshold value
solution: Von Mises: equivalent stress σ_eq = √((σ₁-σ₂)²+(σ₂-σ₃)²+(σ₃-σ₁)²)/√2.
